$comment: The KernelSU manager every target here pairs with. One file, because it is
one manager: nothing about which manager a device gets is a property of
the device.
Upstream's cannot be used. It rewrites /data/adb/ksud with the copy bundled
in its own APK the first time it runs, which puts an unpatched daemon back:
measured on Quest 3, where opening it undid common/0004 and the next soft
restart went back to leaving stale lspd and sui behind, with nothing in any
log to say the daemon had been replaced. A soft restart is the only restart
a late-loaded device has, so that is the normal path and not a corner case.
So this is not an alternative offered alongside upstream's -- it is the
only manager the modules built here will look at. package and signature
below are compiled into every one of them as KSU_MANAGER_PACKAGE and
KSU_EXPECTED_SIZE / KSU_EXPECTED_HASH. Those last two are upstream's own
defaults in kernel/Kbuild, replaced rather than added to, so there is no
second slot left holding upstream's certificate. The official manager is
then not refused on such a device: is_manager_apk() never returns true for
it, so it is never found, and a manager the kernel does not recognise
cannot rewrite ksud. Both can be installed at once.
versionCode and versionName are NOT here. The manager and the module carry
the same number -- the manager shows the pair on its home screen as
<version>-<uapi> and refuses a module below its own
MINIMAL_SUPPORTED_KERNEL -- and that number is the KernelSU submodule pin's
commit count. It is derived from the pin everywhere else and is derived
here too, so a pin move cannot leave the feed advertising the old one. url
is checked for it, which is what catches a release that was not rebuilt.
signature is the DER size and sha256 of the certificate in
Android-Keys/kernelsu-manager. It is not a secret. The build that produces
the APK asserts the same pair against what it actually signed, and the feed
job here downloads the APK and asserts it again -- the two repositories
cannot compare strings across the gap, but they can both check the artifact.
name: Root My Device KSU
note: The official KernelSU manager replaces ksud with its own copy and undoes the fix that keeps modules working across a soft restart, which is the only restart this device has. The module accepts this manager and no other.
